headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: xonsh can read/write files and run shell commands, but awesome-selfhosted is non-runnable and network-egress none, limiting direct pairwise harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no I/O surfaces and is non-runnable, so it cannot directly inject B. B can read files and stdin/stdout, so only a manual copy-paste or file handoff from A’s content into B would create a prompt-injection path. That makes the pathway possible but unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated text into B's stdin/stdout or a shared file
IF B is instructed to treat that copied content as authoritative
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B prompts unless reviewed
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from copied text
Paste only quoted excerpts, not raw content
Add a human review step before B acts on A output

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has network_egress none, while B can read/write the filesystem and has broad network egress. Because A is non-runnable and the pair lacks a shared workspace in the profiles, leakage is not default; the main risk is operator-mediated file transfer into B.
conditions: IF sensitive files are manually placed into B's filesystem context
IF B is used to transmit those files to external services
mitigations: Do not mount sensitive directories into B
Redact secrets before any file handoff
Disable outbound network use during sensitive tasks
Use separate workspaces for A and B

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but modify_git_state is false and A is non-runnable, so there is no meaningful simultaneous write conflict beyond unusual operator-created shared files.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory by the operator
IF B is asked to overwrite files that A also references
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Snapshot the workspace before B runs
Restrict B to read-only mode when possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a knowledge-management list and not runnable, so it does not generate operational facts or actions. B can execute shell commands, but there is no documented pipeline where B consumes A’s output by default. Any cascade would require manual transfer and trust by the operator, making the risk limited.
conditions: IF A’s text is copied into B as instructions or commands
IF B is allowed to execute commands derived from that copied text without verification
mitigations: Require verification before executing copied commands
Separate research output from executable instructions
Use a checklist to validate commands from A
Run B in a dry-run mode first

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for A, and B’s profile lists no secrets handled or regulated data classes. With only docs-only profiles and no evidence of PHI, EU PII, or similar flows, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent’s workflow
IF a separate policy document assigns residency or retention obligations not shown here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
